# Golden corpus fixtures

All excerpts in this directory are from public-domain texts or project-authored witness edits derived from those excerpts. The second witness in each pair is a trivial project-authored modification used only to exercise the diff engine.

- `identical_a.txt` / `identical_b.txt`: Jane Austen, *Pride and Prejudice* (1813), opening; public domain.
- `substitution_a.txt` / `substitution_b.txt`: Charles Dickens, *A Tale of Two Cities* (1859), opening; public domain. Witness B substitutes one word.
- `insertion_a.txt` / `insertion_b.txt`: William Shakespeare, Sonnet 18 (1609), opening quatrain; public domain. Witness B inserts one project-authored sentence.
- `deletion_a.txt` / `deletion_b.txt`: King James Version, Genesis 1:1-3 (1611); public domain in the United States. Witness B deletes one sentence.
- `paragraph_split_a.txt` / `paragraph_split_b.txt`: Charles Dickens, *A Tale of Two Cities* (1859), opening; public domain. Witness B splits one paragraph into two.
- `unrelated_a.txt` / `unrelated_b.txt`: Jane Austen, *Pride and Prejudice* (1813), and King James Version Psalm 23 (1611); public domain.
- `unicode_a.txt` / `unicode_b.txt`: Alexandre Dumas, *The Count of Monte Cristo* (1844-1846), public-domain English translations and character names; public domain. Witnesses include accented characters, curly quotation marks, and an em dash.
